system_prompt:
You are Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research. You are helpful, knowledgeable, and direct. You assist users with a wide range of tasks including answering questions, writing and editing code, analyzing information, creative work, and executing actions via your tools. You communicate clearly, admit uncertainty when appropriate, and prioritize being genuinely useful over being verbose unless otherwise directed below. Be targeted and efficient in your exploration and investigations.

# Tool-use enforcement
You MUST use your tools to take action — do not describe what you would do or plan to do without actually doing it. When you say you will perform an action (e.g. 'I will run the tests', 'Let me check the file', 'I will create the project'), you MUST immediately make the corresponding tool call in the same response. Never end your turn with a promise of future action — execute it now.
Keep working until the task is actually complete. Do not stop with a summary of what you plan to do next time. If you have tools available that can accomplish the task, use them instead of telling the user what you would do.
Every response should either (a) contain tool calls that make progress, or (b) deliver a final result to the user. Responses that only describe intentions without acting are not acceptable.

# Google model operational directives
Follow these operational rules strictly:
- **Absolute paths:** Always construct and use absolute file paths for all file system operations. Combine the project root with relative paths.
- **Verify first:** Use read_file/search_files to check file contents and project structure before making changes. Never guess at file contents.
- **Dependency checks:** Never assume a library is available. Check package.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, etc. before importing.
- **Conciseness:** Keep explanatory text brief — a few sentences, not paragraphs. Focus on actions and results over narration.
- **Parallel tool calls:** When you need to perform multiple independent operations (e.g. reading several files), make all the tool calls in a single response rather than sequentially.
- **Non-interactive commands:** Use flags like -y, --yes, --non-interactive to prevent CLI tools from hanging on prompts.
- **Keep going:** Work autonomously until the task is fully resolved. Don't stop with a plan — execute it.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with line numbers and pagination. Use this instead of cat/head/tail in terminal. Output format: 'LINE_NUM|CONTENT'. Suggests similar filenames if not found. Use offset and limit for large files. Reads exceeding ~100K characters are rejected; use offset and limit to read specific sections of large files. NOTE: Cannot read images or binary files — use vision_analyze for images.

path.description: Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, default: 1)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default: 500, max: 2000)

function.name: search_files
function.description:
Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. Ripgrep-backed, faster than shell equivalents.

Content search (target='content'): Regex search inside files. Output modes: full matches with line numbers, file paths only, or match counts.

File search (target='files'): Find files by glob pattern (e.g., '*.py', '*config*'). Also use this instead of ls — results sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: Regex pattern for content search, or glob pattern (e.g., '*.py') for file search

target.description: 'content' searches inside file contents, 'files' searches for files by name

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default: current working directory)

file_glob.description: Filter files by pattern in grep mode (e.g., '*.py' to only search Python files)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)

offset.description: Skip first N results for pagination (default: 0)

output_mode.description: Output format for grep mode: 'content' shows matching lines with line numbers, 'files_only' lists file paths, 'count' shows match counts per file

context.description: Number of context lines before and after each match (grep mode only)

function.description:
Manage your SESSION-ONLY task list for planning and step-tracking during complex work. This list is ephemeral -- it does NOT persist across sessions.

Use this for: breaking down multi-step tasks, tracking progress within a session.
Use dashboard_task_* tools instead for: real action items, reminders, or anything Brian needs to see on his dashboard or track across sessions.

Call with no parameters to read the current list.

Writing:
- Provide 'todos' array to create/update items
- merge=false (default): replace the entire list with a fresh plan
- merge=true: update existing items by id, add any new ones

Each item: {id: string, content: string, status: pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled}
List order is priority. Only ONE item in_progress at a time.
Mark items completed immediately when done. If something fails, cancel it and add a revised item.

Always returns the full current list.

todos.description: Task items to write. Omit to read current list.

merge.description: true: update existing items by id, add new ones. false (default): replace the entire list.

1. **Force Directory Creation**: `mkdir -p docs/features/export-feature/`
2. **Direct File Creation**: Instead of relying on subagents to "think" and "write", I want you to gather the necessary info first, then write the file using a method that is guaranteed to persist. 
3. **Phase 1 Execution**:
    - Find the data models, permissions, and API routes.
    - Draft the `PLAN.md` content in your context.
    - **Crucially**: Use `delegate_worker` with a goal that explicitly says: "Write the following text to 'docs/features/export-feature/PLAN.md' using a single `write_file` call. Do not use any other method. Here is the content: [DRAFTED CONTENT]"
4. **Verification**: Run `ls -R docs/features/export-feature/` and `read_file` on the path to confirm.

**Target Content for PLAN.md should include**:
- Architecture (Export Service, Transformation Layer, Permission Layer).
- Phase 2 (Core Logic): Data retrieval & transformation (CSV, JSON, PDF).
- Phase 3 (API): Endpoints and OpenAPI updates.
- Phase 4 (Testing): Unit/Integration tests (80%+ coverage).
- Phase 5 (Verification): E2E flow.

If you cannot find the files for Discovery, please search for 'models', 'auth', and 'api' and report what you find before attempting the write.

{"content": "     1|---
     2|sidebar_position: 14
     3|title: "API Server"
     4|description: "Expose hermes-agent as an OpenAI-compatible API for any frontend"
     5|---
     6|
     7|# API Server
     8|
     9|The API server exposes hermes-agent as an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. Any frontend that speaks the OpenAI format — Open WebUI, LobeChat, LibreChat, NextChat, ChatBox, and hundreds more — can connect to hermes-agent and use it as a backend.
    10|
    11|Your agent handles requests with its full toolset (terminal, file operations, web search, memory, skills) and returns the final response. When streaming, tool progress indicators appear inline so frontends can show what the agent is doing.
    12|
    13|## Quick Start
    14|
    15|### 1. Enable the API server
    16|
    17|Add to `~/.hermes/.env`:
    18|
    19|```bash
    20|API_SERVER_ENABLED=true
    21|API_SERVER_KEY=change-me-local-dev
    22|# Optional: only if a browser must call Hermes directly
    23|# API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000
    24|```
    25|
    26|### 2. Start the gateway
    27|
    28|```bash
    29|hermes gateway
    30|```
    31|
    32|You'll see:
    33|
    34|```
    35|[API Server] API server listening on http://127.0.0.1:8642
    36|```
    37|
    38|### 3. Connect a frontend
    39|
    40|Point any OpenAI-compatible client at `http://localhost:8642/v1`:
    41|
    42|```bash
    43|# Test with curl
    44|curl http://localhost:8642/v1/chat/completions \
    45|  -H "Authorization: Bearer change...dev" \
    46|  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    47|  -d '{"model": "hermes-agent", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
    48|```
    49|
    50|Or connect Open WebUI, LobeChat, or any other frontend — see the [Open WebUI integration guide](/docs/user-guide/messaging/open-webui) for step-by-step instructions.
    51|
    52|## Endpoints
    53|
    54|### POST /v1/chat/completions
    55|
    56|Standard OpenAI Chat Completions format. Stateless — the full conversation is included in each request via the `messages` array.
    57|
    58|**Request:**
    59|```json
    60|{
    61|  "model": "hermes-agent",
    62|  "messages": [
    63|    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a Python expert."},
    64|    {"role": "user", "content": "Write a fibonacci function"}
    65|  ],
    66|  "stream": false
    67|}
    68|```
    69|
    70|**Response:**
    71|```json
    72|{
    73|  "id": "chatcmpl-abc123",
    74|  "object": "chat.completion",
    75|  "created": 1710000000,
    76|  "model": "hermes-agent",
    77|  "choices": [{
    78|    "index": 0,
    79|    "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Here's a fibonacci function..."},
    80|    "finish_reason": "stop"
    81|  }],
    82|  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 50, "completion_tokens": 200, "total_tokens": 250}
    83|}
    84|```
    85|
    86|**Streaming** (`"stream": true`): Returns Server-Sent Events (SSE) with token-by-token response chunks. When streaming is enabled in config, tokens are emitted live as the LLM generates them. When disabled, the full response is sent as a single SSE chunk.
    87|
    88|**Tool progress in streams**: When the agent calls tools during a streaming request, brief progress indicators are injected into the content stream as the tools start executing (e.g. `` `💻 pwd` ``, `` `🔍 Python docs` ``). These appear as inline markdown before the agent's response text, giving frontends like Open WebUI real-time visibility into tool execution.
    89|
    90|### POST /v1/responses
    91|
    92|OpenAI Responses API format. Supports server-side conversation state via `previous_response_id` — the server stores full conversation history (including tool calls and results) so multi-turn context is preserved without the client managing it.
    93|
    94|**Request:**
    95|```json
    96|{
    97|  "model": "hermes-agent",
    98|  "input": "What files are in my project?",
    99|  "instructions": "You are a helpful coding assistant.",
   100|  "store": true
   101|}
   102|```
   103|
   104|**Response:**
   105|```json
   106|{
   107|  "id": "resp_abc123",
   108|  "object": "response",
   109|  "status": "completed",
   110|  "model": "hermes-agent",
   111|  "output": [
   112|    {"type": "function_call", "name": "terminal", "arguments": "{\"command\": \"ls\"}", "call_id": "call_1"},
   113|    {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": "README.md src/ tests/"},
   114|    {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Your project has..."}]}
   115|  ],
   116|  "usage": {"input_tokens": 50, "output_tokens": 200, "total_tokens": 250}
   117|}
   118|```
   119|
   120|#### Multi-turn with previous_response_id
   121|
   122|Chain responses to maintain full context (including tool calls) across turns:
   123|
   124|```json
   125|{
   126|  "input": "Now show me the README",
   127|  "previous_response_id": "resp_abc123"
   128|}
   129|```
   130|
   131|The server reconstructs the full conversation from the stored response chain — all previous tool calls and results are preserved.
   132|
   133|#### Named conversations
   134|
   135|Use the `conversation` parameter instead of tracking response IDs:
   136|
   137|```json
   138|{"input": "Hello", "conversation": "my-project"}
   139|{"input": "What's in src/?", "conversation": "my-project"}
   140|{"input": "Run the tests", "conversation": "my-project"}
   141|```
   142|
   143|The server automatically chains to the latest response in that conversation. Like the `/title` command for gateway sessions.
   144|
   145|### GET /v1/responses/\{id\}
   146|
   147|Retrieve a previously stored response by ID.
   148|
   149|### DELETE /v1/responses/\{id\}
   150|
   151|Delete a stored response.
   152|
   153|### GET /v1/models
   154|
   155|Lists `hermes-agent` as an available model. Required by most frontends for model discovery.
   156|
   157|### GET /health
   158|
   159|Health check. Returns `{"status": "ok"}`. Also available at **GET /v1/health** for OpenAI-compatible clients that expect the `/v1/` prefix.
   160|
   161|## System Prompt Handling
   162|
   163|When a frontend sends a `system` message (Chat Completions) or `instructions` field (Responses API), hermes-agent **layers it on top** of its core system prompt. Your agent keeps all its tools, memory, and skills — the frontend's system prompt adds extra instructions.
   164|
   165|This means you can customize behavior per-frontend without losing capabilities:
   166|- Open WebUI system prompt: "You are a Python expert. Always include type hints."
   167|- The agent still has terminal, file tools, web search, memory, etc.
   168|
   169|## Authentication
   170|
   171|Bearer token auth via the `Authorization` header:
   172|
   173|```
   174|Authorization: Bearer ***
   175|```
   176|
   177|Configure the key via `API_SERVER_KEY` env var. If you need a browser to call Hermes directly, also set `API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS` to an explicit allowlist.
   178|
   179|:::warning Security
   180|The API server gives full access to hermes-agent's toolset, **including terminal commands**. If you change the bind address to `0.0.0.0` (network-accessible), **always set `API_SERVER_KEY`** and keep `API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS` narrow — without that, remote callers may be able to execute arbitrary commands on your machine.
   181|
   182|The default bind address (`127.0.0.1`) is for local-only use. Browser access is disabled by default; enable it only for explicit trusted origins.
   183|:::
   184|
   185|## Configuration
   186|
   187|### Environment Variables
   188|
   189|| Variable | Default | Description |
   190||----------|---------|-------------|
   191|| `API_SERVER_ENABLED` | `false` | Enable the API server |
   192|| `API_SERVER_PORT` | `8642` | HTTP server port |
   193|| `API_SERVER_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address (localhost only by default) |
   194|| `API_SERVER_KEY` | _(none)_ | Bearer token for auth |
   195|| `API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS` | _(none)_ | Comma-separated allowed browser origins |
   196|
   197|### config.yaml
   198|
   199|```yaml
   200|# Not yet supported — use environment variables.
   201|# config.yaml support coming in a future release.
   202|```
   203|
   204|## Security Headers
   205|
   206|All responses include security headers:
   207|- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` — prevents MIME type sniffing
   208|- `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` — prevents referrer leakage
   209|
   210|## CORS
   211|
   212|The API server does **not** enable browser CORS by default.
   213|
   214|For direct browser access, set an explicit allowlist:
   215|
   216|```bash
   217|API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000
   218|```
   219|
   220|When CORS is enabled:
   221|- **Preflight responses** include `Access-Control-Max-Age: 600` (10 minute cache)
   222|- **SSE streaming responses** include CORS headers so browser EventSource clients work correctly
   223|- **`Idempotency-Key`** is an allowed request header — clients can send it for deduplication (responses are cached by key for 5 minutes)
   224|
   225|Most documented frontends such as Open WebUI connect server-to-server and do not need CORS at all.
   226|
   227|## Compatible Frontends
   228|
   229|Any frontend that supports the OpenAI API format works. Tested/documented integrations:
   230|
   231|| Frontend | Stars | Connection |
   232||----------|-------|------------|
   233|| [Open WebUI](/docs/user-guide/messaging/open-webui) | 126k | Full guide available |
   234|| LobeChat | 73k | Custom provider endpoint |
   235|| LibreChat | 34k | Custom endpoint in librechat.yaml |
   236|| AnythingLLM | 56k | Generic OpenAI provider |
   237|| NextChat | 87k | BASE_URL env var |
   238|| ChatBox | 39k | API Host setting |
   239|| Jan | 26k | Remote model config |
   240|| HF Chat-UI | 8k | OPENAI_BASE_URL |
   241|| big-AGI | 7k | Custom endpoint |
   242|| OpenAI Python SDK | — | `OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8642/v1")` |
   243|| curl | — | Direct HTTP requests |
   244|
   245|## Limitations
   246|
   247|- **Response storage** — stored responses (for `previous_response_id`) are persisted in SQLite and survive gateway restarts. Max 100 stored responses (LRU eviction).
   248|- **No file upload** — vision/document analysis via uploaded files is not yet supported through the API.
   249|- **Model field is cosmetic** — the `model` field in requests is accepted but the actual LLM model used is configured server-side in config.yaml.
